name: swing-mcp
description: Let AI drive Java Swing desktop apps — see the UI, click, fill forms, read tables. No API needed.
long_description:
**Swing MCP gives AI assistants hands inside Java Swing desktop applications** — the ERP clients, point-of-sale screens, lab and logistics tools and internal apps that run a lot of businesses and have no API.

Once the bundled agent is loaded into the app's JVM (at launch, or by attaching to a running process by PID), Claude can:

- **See the UI** as a structured component tree — every button, field, table, tree, menu and dialog with a stable id — instead of guessing from pixels.
- **Act in it**: click, type, fill fields and spinners, pick combo-box options, select table cells and tree nodes, drive menus and right-click menus, drag, scroll, press keys.
- **Read data out**: whole `JTable` contents, list and tree items, component details, the clipboard, and screenshots of a window or a single component.
- **Handle the awkward parts**: modal dialogs are detected and answered instead of blocking the session; `wait_for` waits for UI conditions; several apps can be driven in parallel sessions.

**Who it's for:** teams that maintain or test Swing software, and anyone who wants an assistant to operate a desktop app that was never built for automation. Typical uses: exploratory and regression UI testing, reproducing bugs, extracting data from screens, and automating repetitive clicks in legacy tools.

**Requirements:** a Java 21+ runtime on your `PATH`. Works on macOS, Windows and Linux. The agent listens on loopback only, requires a per-session token, and `evaluate_java` (arbitrary code in the target JVM) is off unless you switch it on.

**Get started:** ask Claude to `launch_app` with the path to your app's jar (or `attach_to_app` with a running PID), then `take_snapshot` and take it from there. Full tool reference, per-client setup and a demo: https://crosstech.solutions/swing-mcp

Open source (MIT) by CrossTech. Need this connected to your own application, or an MCP connector for other software your business runs? See the link above.
